521	func promotePreparedHistoryProjection(outputDir string, prepared *preparedHistoryProjection) error {
522		if prepared == nil || prepared.stagingDir == "" || prepared.generation == "" {
523			return errors.New("history projection staging identity is missing")
524		}
525		if !validHistoryGenerationArtifactPath(prepared.indexPath, historyIndexFileName) ||
526			!validHistoryGenerationArtifactPath(prepared.receiptPath, projectionStateFileName) {
527			return errors.New("history projection generation path is invalid")
528		}
529		if err := recoverHistoryProjectionQuarantines(outputDir); err != nil {
530			return fmt.Errorf("recover interrupted history projection cleanup: %w", err)
531		}
532		finalRel := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(historyGenerationsDir, prepared.generation))
533		wantStagingRel := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(historyStagingDir, prepared.generation))
534		if prepared.stagingDir != wantStagingRel || !validHistoryProjectionDirectoryPath(prepared.stagingDir) || !validHistoryProjectionDirectoryPath(finalRel) {
535			return errors.New("history projection directory path is invalid")
536		}
537		staging := filepath.Join(outputDir, filepath.FromSlash(prepared.stagingDir))
538		final := filepath.Join(outputDir, filepath.FromSlash(finalRel))
539		if err := clibase.RejectExistingSymlinkPathComponents(outputDir, historyStagingDir); err != nil {
540			return err
541		}
542		if err := clibase.RejectExistingSymlinkPathComponents(outputDir, historyGenerationsDir); err != nil {
543			return err
544		}
545		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(final), 0o700); err != nil {
546			return err
547		}
548		if err := validateHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, prepared.stagingDir, true); err != nil {
549			return fmt.Errorf("validate staged history generation: %w", err)
550		}
551		if info, err := os.Lstat(final); err == nil {
552			if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.IsDir() {
553				return fmt.Errorf("history projection generation must be an exact directory, not a symlink or special file: %s", finalRel)
554			}
555			manifest, manifestErr := bmanifest.Load(outputDir)
556			if manifestErr != nil {
557				return manifestErr
558			}
559			if manifest.Sources != nil && manifest.Sources.History != nil {
560				currentSource := manifest.Sources.History
561				referencesFinal := filepath.ToSlash(currentSource.IndexPath) == prepared.indexPath || filepath.ToSlash(currentSource.ProjectionStatePath) == prepared.receiptPath
562				if referencesFinal {
563					if _, indexErr := loadBrainHistoryIndex(outputDir, currentSource); indexErr != nil {
564						return fmt.Errorf("current history generation is unreadable and was left untouched: %w", indexErr)
565					}
566					if _, receiptState, receiptErr := loadProjectionStateChecked(outputDir, currentSource); receiptState != projectionStateCurrent {
567						if receiptErr != nil {
568							return receiptErr
569						}
570						return fmt.Errorf("current history generation has %s projection receipts and was left untouched", receiptState)
571					}
572					if err := removeHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, prepared.stagingDir); err != nil {
573						return fmt.Errorf("discard duplicate staged history generation: %w", err)
574					}
575					return nil
576				}
577			}
578			// An unreferenced directory is an orphan from an interrupted publish.
579			// Quarantine and remove it only after proving that it contains no
580			// symlinks, special files, or unknown content.
581			if err := removeHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, finalRel); err != nil {
582				return fmt.Errorf("replace orphaned history generation: %w", err)
583			}
584		} else if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
585			return err
586		}
587		// Re-check immediately before the rename. If an untrusted actor replaced
588		// staging after preparation, the manifest must remain on the prior
589		// generation and no path below the replacement may be touched.
590		if err := validateHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, prepared.stagingDir, true); err != nil {
591			return fmt.Errorf("validate staged history generation at promotion: %w", err)
592		}
593		if err := os.Rename(staging, final); err != nil {
594			return fmt.Errorf("promote history generation: %w", err)
595		}
596		if err := validateHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, finalRel, true); err != nil {
597			return fmt.Errorf("validate promoted history generation: %w", err)
598		}
599		return nil
600	}

602	func discardPreparedHistoryProjection(outputDir string, prepared *preparedHistoryProjection) error {
603		if prepared == nil || prepared.stagingDir == "" {
604			return nil
605		}
606		var cleanupErr error
607		if err := removeHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, prepared.stagingDir); err != nil {
608			cleanupErr = err
609		}
610		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(outputDir)
611		if err == nil && manifest.Sources != nil && manifest.Sources.History != nil &&
612			filepath.ToSlash(manifest.Sources.History.IndexPath) == prepared.indexPath {
613			return cleanupErr
614		}
615		finalRel := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(historyGenerationsDir, prepared.generation))
616		if err := removeHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, finalRel); err != nil && cleanupErr == nil {
617			cleanupErr = err
618		}
619		return cleanupErr
620	}
621	
622	func pruneInactiveHistoryGenerations(outputDir string) {
623		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(outputDir)
624		if err != nil || manifest.Sources == nil || manifest.Sources.History == nil {
625			return
626		}
627		// Never enumerate or remove below an aliased history directory. This check
628		// covers both legacy fixed-path cleanup and the generations root.
629		if err := clibase.RejectExistingSymlinkPathComponents(outputDir, brainstore.HistoryDirName); err != nil {
630			return
631		}
632		if err := recoverHistoryProjectionQuarantines(outputDir); err != nil {
633			return
634		}
635		active := filepath.ToSlash(strings.TrimSpace(manifest.Sources.History.IndexPath))
636		activeReceipt := filepath.ToSlash(strings.TrimSpace(manifest.Sources.History.ProjectionStatePath))
637		if active != historyIndexPath {
638			_ = os.Remove(filepath.Join(outputDir, filepath.FromSlash(historyIndexPath)))
639		}
640		if activeReceipt != projectionStateRel {
641			legacyReceipt := filepath.Join(outputDir, filepath.FromSlash(projectionStateRel))
642			newer, schemaErr := projectionFileHasNewerSchema(legacyReceipt)
643			if schemaErr == nil && !newer {
644				_ = os.Remove(legacyReceipt)
645			}
646		}
647		activeParts := strings.Split(active, "/")
648		if len(activeParts) != 4 || !validHistoryGenerationArtifactPath(active, historyIndexFileName) {
649			return
650		}
651		if err := rejectSymlinkPathComponents(outputDir, historyGenerationsDir); err != nil {
652			return
653		}
654		directory, err := brainstore.ReadMemoryStateDirectory(outputDir, historyGenerationsDir, "history generation directory", brainstore.MemoryStateInventoryMaxEntries)
655		if err != nil || directory.Truncated {
656			return
657		}
658		entries := directory.Entries
659		for _, entry := range entries {
660			generation := entry.Name()
661			candidateIndex := historyGenerationArtifactPath(generation, historyIndexFileName)
662			if generation == activeParts[2] || !validHistoryGenerationArtifactPath(candidateIndex, historyIndexFileName) {
663				continue
664			}
665			dirRel := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(historyGenerationsDir, generation))
666			dir := filepath.Join(outputDir, filepath.FromSlash(dirRel))
667			if err := validateHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, dirRel, false); err != nil {
668				continue
669			}
670			receiptPath := filepath.Join(dir, projectionStateFileName)
671			newer, schemaErr := projectionFileHasNewerSchema(receiptPath)
672			if newer || (schemaErr != nil && !errors.Is(schemaErr, clibase.ErrFileHardlinked)) {
673				continue // unknown-newer generations are never removed by this binary
674			}
675			// A hardlinked receipt is unreadable here forever, and removal only
676			// unlinks this directory's name — the other link keeps the bytes.
677			_ = removeHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, dirRel)
678		}
679	}
680	
681	func projectionFileHasNewerSchema(path string) (bool, error) {
682		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
683		if err != nil {
684			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
685				return false, nil
686			}
687			return false, err
688		}
689		if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
690			return false, fmt.Errorf("projection receipt must be a regular file and must not be a symlink: %s", path)
691		}
692		f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_RDONLY|clibase.FileLockOpenFlags()|clibase.MemoryStateReadOpenFlags(), 0)
693		if err != nil {
694			return false, err
695		}
696		defer f.Close()
697		if err := clibase.RejectOpenFileAlias(path, f, "projection receipt"); err != nil {
698			return false, err
699		}
700		data, err := clibase.SafeReadAll(f, clibase.MaxManifestBytes, path)
701		if err != nil {
702			return false, err
703		}
704		var header struct {
705			SchemaVersion int `json:"schema_version"`
706		}
707		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &header); err != nil || header.SchemaVersion < 1 {
708			return false, fmt.Errorf("projection receipt has an unreadable schema header: %s", path)
709		}
710		return header.SchemaVersion > projectionSchemaVersion, nil
711	}
712	
713	// validHistoryProjectionDirectoryPath accepts only an exact immutable
714	// generation or staging directory. Cleanup never operates on an arbitrary
715	// caller-supplied subtree.
716	func validHistoryProjectionDirectoryPath(rel string) bool {
717		parts := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(rel), "/")
718		if len(parts) != 3 || parts[0] != brainstore.HistoryDirName || (parts[1] != "generations" && parts[1] != "staging") || len(parts[2]) != 40 {
719			return false
720		}
721		_, err := hex.DecodeString(parts[2])
722		return err == nil
723	}
724	
725	// validateHistoryProjectionDirectory uses Lstat for the directory and each
726	// child. Only the two immutable projection artifacts are recognized; a
727	// symlink, special file, or unknown name makes the directory untouchable.
728	func validateHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, rel string, requireComplete bool) error {
729		if !validHistoryProjectionDirectoryPath(rel) {
730			return fmt.Errorf("invalid history projection directory: %s", rel)
731		}
732		parentRel := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(filepath.FromSlash(rel)))
733		if err := clibase.RejectExistingSymlinkPathComponents(outputDir, parentRel); err != nil {
734			return err
735		}
736		abs := filepath.Join(outputDir, filepath.FromSlash(rel))
737		_, _, err := inspectHistoryProjectionDirectory(abs, rel, requireComplete)
738		return err
739	}
740	
741	func inspectHistoryProjectionDirectory(abs, display string, requireComplete bool) (os.FileInfo, []string, error) {
742		info, err := os.Lstat(abs)
743		if err != nil {
744			return nil, nil, err
745		}
746		if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.IsDir() {
747			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("history projection path must be a directory and must not be a symlink: %s", display)
748		}
749		dir, err := os.OpenFile(abs, os.O_RDONLY|clibase.FileLockOpenFlags()|clibase.MemoryStateReadOpenFlags(), 0)
750		if err != nil {
751			return nil, nil, err
752		}
753		defer dir.Close()
754		opened, err := dir.Stat()
755		if err != nil || !opened.IsDir() || !os.SameFile(info, opened) {
756			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("history projection directory changed while opening: %s", display)
757		}
758		entries, err := dir.ReadDir(3)
759		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
760			return nil, nil, err
761		}
762		found := map[string]bool{}
763		names := make([]string, 0, len(entries))
764		for _, entry := range entries {
765			name := entry.Name()
766			if name != historyIndexFileName && name != projectionStateFileName {
767				return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("history projection directory contains unknown entry %q: %s", name, display)
768			}
769			childInfo, err := entry.Info()
770			if err != nil {
771				return nil, nil, err
772			}
773			if childInfo.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !childInfo.Mode().IsRegular() {
774				return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("history projection artifact must be a regular file and must not be a symlink: %s", filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(display, name)))
775			}
776			found[name] = true
777			names = append(names, name)
778		}
779		if requireComplete && (!found[historyIndexFileName] || !found[projectionStateFileName]) {
780			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("history projection directory is incomplete: %s", display)
781		}
782		current, err := os.Lstat(abs)
783		if err != nil || current.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !os.SameFile(opened, current) {
784			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("history projection directory changed during inspection: %s", display)
785		}
786		return info, names, nil
787	}
788	
789	// removeHistoryProjectionDirectory first renames the exact directory to an
790	// inert sibling. Renaming a hostile symlink moves the link itself rather than
791	// traversing its target; the subsequent Lstat validation therefore cannot
792	// delete an external canary. Unknown content is restored and left untouched.
793	func removeHistoryProjectionDirectory(outputDir, rel string) error {
794		if !validHistoryProjectionDirectoryPath(rel) {
795			return fmt.Errorf("refuse cleanup of invalid history projection directory: %s", rel)
796		}
797		parentRel := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(filepath.FromSlash(rel)))
798		if err := clibase.RejectExistingSymlinkPathComponents(outputDir, parentRel); err != nil {
799			return err
800		}
801		abs := filepath.Join(outputDir, filepath.FromSlash(rel))
802		info, err := os.Lstat(abs)
803		if err != nil {
804			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
805				return nil
806			}
807			return err
808		}
809		if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.IsDir() {
810			return fmt.Errorf("refuse cleanup of symlink or non-directory history projection: %s", rel)
811		}
812		// Prove the SHAPE while the directory is still at its published path: a
813		// projection generation holds exactly index.json and the receipt, both
814		// regular files. This is the check that decides whether the directory is
815		// safe to delete, and it runs before anything is moved.
816		if _, _, err := inspectHistoryProjectionDirectory(abs, rel, false); err != nil {
817			return err
818		}
819		quarantine := abs + ".removing"
820		if _, err := os.Lstat(quarantine); err == nil {
821			return fmt.Errorf("history projection cleanup quarantine already exists: %s", filepath.ToSlash(rel)+".removing")
822		} else if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
823			return err
824		}
825		if err := os.Rename(abs, quarantine); err != nil {
826			return err
827		}
828		restore := func(cause error) error {
829			if _, currentErr := os.Lstat(abs); os.IsNotExist(currentErr) {
830				if renameErr := os.Rename(quarantine, abs); renameErr != nil {
831					return fmt.Errorf("%v (also could not restore quarantined projection: %w)", cause, renameErr)
832				}
833			}
834			return cause
835		}
836		// Re-prove the shape at the quarantine path. Identity is deliberately NOT
837		// compared across the rename: os.Lstat resolves file identity lazily by
838		// PATH on Windows, so the pre-rename FileInfo re-resolves against a path
839		// that no longer exists and os.SameFile is unconditionally false there.
840		// That made this cleanup a permanent no-op on Windows, which is what left
841		// unreferenced generations behind for privacy verification to find. The
842		// rename itself is the atomic step that carries identity: it moved exactly

# Longest-first to avoid prefix collisions.
pairs = [
    ("loadBrainHistoryIndexWithLegacyIdentity(", "historystore.LoadIndexWithLegacyIdentity("),
    ("loadBrainHistoryIndex(", "historystore.LoadIndex("),
    ("decodeBrainHistoryIndex(", "historystore.DecodeIndex("),
    ("validateHistoryIndexPath(", "historystore.ValidateIndexPath("),
    ("validHistoryGenerationArtifactPath(", "historystore.ValidGenerationArtifactPath("),
    ("validHistoryStagingArtifactPath(", "historystore.ValidStagingArtifactPath("),
    ("historyGenerationArtifactPath(", "historystore.GenerationArtifactPath("),
    ("historyIndexReadError(", "historystore.IndexReadError("),
    ("historyHardlinkRepairHint(", "historystore.HardlinkRepairHint("),
    ("historyRecordsFingerprint(", "historystore.RecordsFingerprint("),
    ("historyIndexBytesFingerprint(", "historystore.IndexBytesFingerprint("),
    ("validHistorySHA256(", "historystore.ValidSHA256("),
    ("historySourceNeedsIdentityUpgrade(", "historystore.SourceNeedsIdentityUpgrade("),
    ("deriveHistoryLegacyIdentity(", "historystore.DeriveLegacyIdentity("),
    (".sourceWithIdentity(", ".SourceWithIdentity("),
    ("historyIndexFileName", "historystore.IndexFileName"),
    ("historyGenerationsDir", "historystore.GenerationsDir"),
    ("historyStagingDir", "historystore.StagingDir"),
    (".recordsFingerprint", ".RecordsFingerprint"),
    (".storageIdentity", ".StorageIdentity"),
    ("storageIdentity:", "StorageIdentity:"),
    ("recordsFingerprint:", "RecordsFingerprint:"),
]
# historyIndexPath: const only; avoid validateHistoryIndexPath (handled above,
# different case) and any longer identifiers. Use word-boundary regex.
ident_pairs = [
    (re.compile(r"\bhistoryIndexPath\b"), "historystore.IndexPath"),
]

changed = []
for f in glob.glob("internal/cli/*.go"):
    src = open(f).read()
    orig = src
    for old, new in pairs:
        src = src.replace(old, new)
    for rx, new in ident_pairs:
        src = rx.sub(new, src)
    if src != orig:
        open(f, "w").write(src)
        changed.append(f)
print("\n".join(sorted(changed)))

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
